Thought: The Beckmann rearrangement is an organic reaction that converts ketoximes to amides. In this reaction, the ketoxime undergoes a rearrangement in the presence of an acid catalyst, where the group opposite to the hydroxyl group migrates to the nitrogen, resulting in the formation of an amide. This is a classic name reaction in organic chemistry.

The general reaction is:
R1-C(=N-OH)-R2 → R1-NH-C(=O)-R2

So the product of the acid-catalyzed Beckmann rearrangement of ketoximes is an amide, which corresponds to option A.
